working_title: England's Undiscovered Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing Northumberland
angle: Northumberland's coastal strip packs in a remarkable concentration of links and clifftop courses within a 20-mile stretch, yet it rarely appears on the bucket lists that send UK golfers straight to Scotland or Ireland. This post makes the practical case for a Northumberland golf trip: the key courses, how to sequence them, visitor logistics, and why the county deserves far more attention than it gets.
research_notes:
- Northumberland has over 30 golf courses in total, with 7 links or downland courses along the coast alone (northumberlandsgolfcoast.com)
- Within roughly 20 miles of coastline there is a dense cluster of seaside courses including Bamburgh Castle, Dunstanburgh Castle, Alnmouth, Alnmouth Village, Seahouses, and Goswick Links (littlehideaways.co.uk)
- Bamburgh Castle Golf Club: 18-hole clifftop links, par 68, 5,645 yards, established 1904. Known for views of Bamburgh Castle, the Farne Islands, and Holy Island (Lindisfarne). Course lined with gorse, heather, and basalt rock. Visitors welcome but Saturdays reserved for member competitions; tee times before 10am also reserved for members. Club is now cashless (bamburghcastlegolfclub.co.uk, tripadvisor.co.uk)
- Bamburgh, Alnmouth, and Goswick run a 'Coastal Golf Classics' package: three contrasting seaside rounds for £150 per person (bamburghcastlegolfclub.co.uk) — NOTE: do not link this as an affiliate; mention informationally only
- Dunstanburgh Castle Golf Club: 18-hole links wrapping around Embleton Bay, designed by James Braid, founded 1900. Set in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, adjacent to 14th-century castle ruins. Open to the public, visitor-friendly with food and drink in the clubhouse (visitnorthumberland.com, dunstanburgh.com)
- Alnmouth Golf Club: described as the 4th oldest golf club in England, established 1869. Par 71, 6,525 yards (men). Course redesigned by H.S. Colt in 1930. Coastal parkland turf rather than pure links. Has a 26-bed dormy house for stay-and-play. Visitors welcome every day except Saturday; advance booking essential; handicap certificate required. Situated less than an hour from Newcastle via the A1 (alnmouthgolfclub.com, visitnorthumberland.com)
- Alnmouth Village Golf Club: separate club from Alnmouth GC, 9-hole/18-tee links layout designed by Mungo Park in 1869, par 71, 6,090 yards. Welcomes visiting golfers (alnmouth.village.golf)
- Goswick Links: James Braid design, recognised by the R&A as an Open qualifying course (alnmouthgolfclub.com)
- The area sits comfortably between Newcastle and the Scottish border, and is noted as being in easy reach of East Lothian's golf coast across the border (dunstanburgh.com) — making it a logical add-on for a wider Scotland/England road trip
- Both the European Tour and Senior Tour have held events in Northumberland (visitnorthumberland.com)
- Northumberland Coast designated an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty; heritage features include Bamburgh Castle, Dunstanburgh Castle ruins, Holy Island/Lindisfarne, and the Farne Islands
- Practical visitor note: Bamburgh Castle GC reserves Saturday tee times for members and blocks early morning slots for visitors; Alnmouth GC closed to visitors on Saturdays; advance booking strongly advised at all clubs
- No specific green fees confirmed for Bamburgh (website lists seasonal pricing tiers but figures not scraped); Alnmouth GC guide price around £60 per round midweek per Golfshake — treat as approximate, check direct
- A 2-night/3-round package (Bamburgh + Goswick + Dunstanburgh) with local hotel accommodation was advertised from around £190pp in June 2026 (golfoffers.uk) — do not state as current or guaranteed; mention that packages exist and to check direct
must_avoid:

- Do not claim first-hand experience playing any of these courses
- Do not invent quotes from golfers, reviewers, or pros
- No gambling, betting, health/injury, or financial advice content
- No affiliate links unless the clubs/operators appear in approved-partners.md; mention any packages or booking operators as informational only with no link
- No em dashes anywhere in the post
- UK English spelling throughout (honour, recognise, etc.)
- Do not duplicate the East Lothian angle already covered in scotland-s-golf-coast-a-practical-guide-to-playing-east-lothian (though a brief cross-reference to East Lothian as a natural companion trip is fine)
- Saturday visitor restrictions at both Bamburgh and Alnmouth GC must be flagged clearly so readers do not plan around a Saturday tee time
